- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.6), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is trending up.  
- If model shows a sharp spike followed by a forecast drop, it often overshoots; cap the peak forecast at 1.5x recent high.  
- If true outcome consistently lags model by 1–2 days, apply a 0.5–1.0% downward correction to the 30-day forecast starting from day 10.  
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +1.5 to -1.0), model often misreads momentum; apply a 1–2% mean-reversion adjustment to the 14-day forecast.  
- When sentiment is neutral (±0.2) and price is volatile, model tends to overfit short-term noise; use 30-day moving average as a smoothing anchor.
